posts.title: Play review: Controlled Burn at Camden Fringe
posts.description: Controlled Burn, presented at Camden People’s Theatre during Camden Fringe, explores a family’s complex dynamics through one performer portraying two sisters and their controlling mother. Using shifting perspectives, monologues, recordings, and symbolic wildfire imagery, Crystalsia Varelis examines storytelling, family myths, identity, and emotional repression. posts.title: Voila Theatre Festival review: Principessa at Barons Court
posts.description: Lauren Easton’s Principessa, inspired by Roman Holiday, follows idealistic American Ann as she seeks romance in Rome with Marco. Performed solo in a simple staging, the show warmly embraces classic screen-romance conventions through music, humour, and heartfelt storytelling. posts.title: Event review: Overture at House of Burlesque, QT Covent Garden
posts.description: House of Burlesque’s Overture is a lively, theatrical celebration of women, history, and body positivity at Covent Garden’s QT hotel. Featuring eight performers, comedy, poetry, dance, music, audience participation, and playful striptease, the three-hour show is energetic and welcoming. Despite some obstructed views and costly drinks, it delivers an entertaining, empowering night out. The post Eve
